key_insight: A coupled generative-predictive workflow can overcome the extreme sparsity of singlet fission candidates and rapidly discover molecules that satisfy stringent excited-state energy criteria.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a scalable inverse-design route for excited-state functional materials, reducing trial-and-error screening and accelerating photovoltaic materials discovery.
method: Use a structure generator to propose new molecules in chemical space.
Apply predictive models to score singlet fission energetic criteria.
Validate promising candidates with a multi-criteria workflow including TDDFT and synthetic accessibility checks.
evidence_signal: The study screened about 100 million generated structures and reported a 90.8% success rate for singlet fission candidates in a TDDFT-validated 1% random subset.
watch_item: The reported performance depends on model-guided generation and limited TDDFT validation, so broader experimental confirmation and robustness across unseen chemistries remain necessary.
paper_title: Navigating Sparse Singlet Fission Chemical Space: An Intelligent Generative-Predictive Paradigm
